The volume of total crude oil and petroleum product imports fell in November to 248.1 million barrels from 288.4 million barrels in October. The total value fell to $5.43 billion in November from $6.27 billion. These data are available only on a Census basis.

The price of imported crude oil rose to an average $21.44 a barrel in November, the highest level since January 1991, from $21.38 per barrel in October. The value of November crude oil imports fell to $4.11 billion from $4.81 billion.

The balance-of-payments basis for recording U.S. trade via receipts from and payments to other countries includes adjustments for military shipments, nonmonetary gold, and inland freight trade with Canada and Mexico.
Census basis data uses information collected by the U.S. Customs Service on goods shipped across U.S. borders.
The drop in the U.S. trade deficit with China in November was the first monthly decline in seven months and brought the gap to its lowest level since April of 1996.
Exports to China rose to a record $1.58 billion, helped by stepped-up shipments of soybeans, while imports from China tumbled by $1.24 billion after the end of pre-Christmas stocking by U.S. stores.
The U.S. trade deficit with Canada rose 34 percent in November as imports of cars and trucks rebounded following the end of a strike at General Motors Corp factories in Canada.
The trade gap with Japan through the first 11 months of 1996 was $43.42 billion, down 22 percent from same period a year earlier and the lowest since 1991.
